title: PRG 292 Taro (PSB G 5): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: PRG 292 Taro: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: PRG 292 taro is a taro variety. About 8 months to harvest, 5.2 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: PRG 292 is a registered taro variety, also sold or known as PSB G 5. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Gb 05. It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest, with 5.24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.caption: Key facts of PRG 292
rows: Tall and upright slender petiole, produce rhizomes

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

PRG 292 taro takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 10 taro varieties with a day count, 8 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 5.24 t/ha trails the average of its group, 8.82. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.
The pests and diseases that hit taro fields most often: [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have white flesh and purple brown skin. Dry matter is 40.59 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. It is recommended for food.
Where and when to plant PRG 292 taro
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Gabi grows in wet lowland or on upland beds. Pick a variety for the land you have, and for the corm, the leaves or both.

items.q: Is PSB G 5 the same as PRG 292?
items.a: Yes. PSB G 5 is another name for PRG 292, registered as NSIC 2000 Gb 05. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 5.24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of PRG 292?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
